newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress to back Gujral on budget vote.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress to back Gujral on budget vote.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Tuesday it would not allow Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's minority coalition government to fall in a budget vote due to be taken next month.

Congress leader Pranab Mukherjee told a news conference his party, which provides make-or-break support to Gujral's 15-party alliance, would help the government in defeating any move by the opposition, or by Gujral's leftist allies, to amend the budget. "We have some reservations about the budget but we will not help any move that will lead to the fall of the government," Mukherjee said after a meeting with Congress president Sitaram Kesri.
He said the party would not support motions or amendments by other parties. "But we will talk to the government to see if it will make changes on its own."
The Congress wants higher allocation for the energy sector and opposes a reduction of customs duties on certain items that would hurt the domestic industry, Mukherjee said.
The communist-led Left Front controls 52 deputies out of the United Front's 178 members in the lower house of parliament, the 545-seat Lok Sabha.
Congress has 140 members and the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) controls 194 deputies.
Mukherjee said Congress leaders planned to meet Gujral on May 5 to discuss the budget, due to be debated in parliament during a session starting on Wednesday.
Sharad Pawar, Congress leader in the lower house, told reporters that the Finance Bill, which includes tax and tariff proposals, would come up for a vote on May 12.
Last week, Gujral's cabinet adopted the 1997/98 budget which former finance minister P. Chidambaram presented to parliament on February 28.
The Left Front, comprising the two main communist parties, the Revolutionary Socialist Party and the Forward Bloc, decided on Monday to urge the government to modify the budget.
The Left Front issued a statement after a meeting calling for changes in the areas of insurance, taxes, divestment in state enterprises, public distribution, customs duties and excise duties.
The parties said they were opposed to opening up the health insurance sector to private firms.

The United News of India quoted former BJP president Murli Manohar Joshi as saying his party would move about 40 amendments to Chidambaram's budget, including a demand to reduce excise and customs duties on bulk drugs.
The budget was widely applauded by economists and sparked a stock market rally after it was unveiled in February by the previous administration of H.D. Deve Gowda.
